notes:
I couldn't write any notes on John 17 this time. My research tool hit its usage limit before I had read a single page, so I have no sources behind anything I could say about these verses.

The one fetch I tried, the Enduring Word page for John 17, was refused because the tool only opens addresses that first come up in a search. When I then tried to run the searches, the tool reported that I had no calls left for this turn. My other tools have no internet access.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. Notes written from memory would break those rules, so I've left them out.

**What to do next:** ask again in a new message, which should reset the limit. I'll aim to use fewer calls. The plan:

1. **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:** Enduring Word, plus Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on BibleHub or StudyLight, and Precept Austin.
2. **Verses where Protestant traditions differ:**
   - v. 2, 6, 9 and 24 ("those You have given Me"): what this means for election, and whether Jesus prays only for believers (v. 9). Reformed sources such as Ligonier, Monergism and GTY, against Wesleyan sources such as Wesley's Notes and Seedbed.
   - v. 12 ("son of destruction"): what it means for whether believers can fall away for good.
   - v. 17–19 (sanctification): Wesleyan and Holiness teaching against Reformed and Lutheran teaching.
   - v. 21–23 (unity): how different churches apply this prayer for unity.
3. **Other views:**
   - The NET Bible notes for modern scholarship.
   - Augustine's sermons on John (Tractates 104–111) and other Church Fathers on New Advent.
   - Catholic.com and OCA on unity (v. 21) and on sanctification and "glory" (v. 22).
   - Any GotQuestions or GTY pages on how popular modern teaching uses v. 22 ("the glory You gave Me").

If you'd like it done in stages, I can cover v. 1–8 first.
